title: DeFAb: A Dataset for Grounded Scientific Discovery through Defeasible Abduction
abstract: arXiv:2606.18557v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A theory can accommodate a counterexample by adding an exception. The harder problem is deciding how far the exception should extend and which predictions should survive. We present DeFAb, a dataset and symbolic verification framework built from curated biological knowledge in the Gene Ontology. Models fill gaps in a theory or propose exceptions to its rules. A verifier checks the consequences of each edit, allowing different solutions to receive credit. Simple symbolic repairs solve all 336 tasks in the released evaluation panel. This result exposes a limitation of the revision test. An exception tied to one entity can succeed without identifying a pattern that applies to other cases. We develop a contextual task that requires an exception to reach the relevant cases and preserve predictions elsewhere. Two planned studies compare training with verified and rejected examples, and revision with and without feedback about consequences.

translated_title: DeFAb：一个通过可废止溯因实现有据科学发现的数据集
translated_abstract: 一个理论可以通过添加例外来容纳反例，而更难的问题在于决定例外应该扩展到多大范围，以及哪些预测应当得以保留。我们提出了DeFAb，这是一个基于基因本体（Gene Ontology）中经过整理的生物学知识构建的数据集和符号验证框架。模型需要填补理论中的空白，或对其规则提出例外。验证器会检查每次修改的后果，允许多种不同的解决方案获得认可。简单的符号修复即可解决已发布评估面板中的全部336个任务。这一结果暴露了修订测试的一个局限性：与单个实体绑定的例外即使没有识别出适用于其他情况的模式，也可能成功通过测试。为此，我们开发了一个情境化任务，要求所提出的例外能够触及相关案例，同时在其他地方保留原有的预测。我们计划开展两项研究，分别比较使用经验证和被拒绝的示例进行训练的效果，以及修订过程中有和没有后果反馈的差异。
tldr: 该论文提出了基于基因本体构建的DeFAb数据集与符号验证框架，用于评估模型通过可废止溯因修订科学理论的能力，并揭示了现有修订测试无法检验例外泛化性的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DeFAb, a dataset and symbolic verification framework built from the Gene Ontology for evaluating models' theory revision through defeasible abduction, while exposing the limitation that existing revision tests fail to check whether exceptions generalize beyond a single entity.
